audit.evidence: Boots the REAL published TWiki per version (tarballs fetched at build from the SourceForge archive: TWiki-4.3.0/4.3.1/4.3.2.tgz) on Debian + Apache2 mod_cgi + Perl 5.36, running TWiki's OWN bin/ + lib/ tree (RcsLite store, TemplateLogin sessions, HtPasswd auth). The save-CSRF guard executed is TWiki's own lib/TWiki/UI/Save.pm (post_method_only method check) + lib/TWiki/UI.pm verifyCryptToken -- NOT lifted, NOT reimplemented. Only a security-neutral Perl 5.36 portability rewrite is applied at build (wrap `foreach $x qw(...)` lists in parens; drop `defined @array` in setlib.cfg); the CSRF predicates are byte-for-byte unchanged. Attack is an EXTERNAL HTTP forged /bin/save riding the victim admin's TWIKISID cookie. Live gate on real Docker (python3 oracle.py --run-gate): forged GET save reveals flag@v0, blocked post_method_only@v1; tokenless forged POST reveals flag@v1, blocked invalidtoken@v2. passed=true; _residual_blocked_on_v2=true; _seed_blocked_on_v2=true.

flag.placement: compose entrypoint writes ${PCB_FLAG} into the admin-only topic Main.PcbSecret; a guard-passing forged save writes %INCLUDE{"Main.PcbSecret"}% into a page, and the victim admin's own view of that page surfaces the flag. No TWiki business code is instrumented.
